'2027 and beyond' supplies no final deadline, so the horizon is open. limitations: This is a temporary failure of the qualifying condition, not a finding that the forecast is inherently uncheckable.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Data centers getting GPUs from 2027 onward will face billions of dollars in extra costs because of NVIDIA's price increases.

statement.excerpt: This means that any data center with GPUs delivered in 2027 and beyond will now have to cover billions of dollars’ worth of extra costs

from_speaker: billions of dollars’ worth of extra costs
our_interpretation: Read 'any data center' as a facility-level assertion about each qualifying data center, rather than an industry-wide aggregate.
Read 'billions' as at least two billion US dollars in incremental costs attributable to the described price increases.
Compare like-for-like procurement costs before and after the increase, holding quantities and configurations constant.
'2027 and beyond' gives an earliest delivery year but no final deadline.
Treat delivery in 2027 or later as the stated qualifying condition. That condition cannot yet have occurred at the evaluation date.
criteria.support_condition: For qualifying deliveries, facility-level procurement records establish at least USD 2 billion in additional costs attributable to the described price increases. A few large projects alone cannot establish the universal wording.
criteria.contradiction_condition: One qualifying facility's complete procurement records establish incremental costs below USD 2 billion on the same scope and comparison basis.
